summary: Client region-tag mismatch routing customer traffic to remote egress causing increased tail latency and intermittent timeouts
description:
Issue summary:

Mapora Analytics has reported sustained p95/p99 inference latency spikes and intermittent 504 timeouts starting 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC for traffic coming from their EU tenant. Traffic is consistently being routed through a US-east egress path for a subset of account tokens; requests routed via that path show a significant tail latency (p99 > 5s) and occasional streaming disconnects.

Impact:
- Customer reports degraded service in production for 3% of requests, spike concentrated on long-context chat sessions.
- SLO breaches for Mapora (dedicated) on latency and availability.
- Observed increase in downstream cost due to additional retries and cross-region egress.

Environment:
- Redwood prod (customer-dedicated capacity in eu-west).
- Affected routing span appears eu-west -> us-east egress.
- Observed on both rw-instruct-13b-quantized and openchat-7b serving pools.

Steps to reproduce (customer-facing):
1) Send streaming chat request with 4096-token context to endpoint using account token A (Mapora).
2) Observe p95/p99 response times; reproduces with 1/30 requests hitting >3s p95, and 1/500 hitting >5s or timing out.
3) When observed, check request headers for x-redwood-egress and x-pop-affinity.

Logs / Observations:
- x-redwood-egress header sometimes shows us-east-pop-12 despite eu-west routing policy.
- KV cache miss rate for affected requests is ~3x baseline for that account during spikes.
- Trace IDs show additional hop through cross-region egress proxy which adds ~120-180ms RT, but end-to-end tail suggests queueing/batching delays on remote pop.
- No recent deploys to serving runtime in eu-west cluster during window; control plane routing weight change occurred 2026-03-09 21:45 UTC (automated rebalancer job).
- Netflow/peering graphs show brief BGP path-change around the same time (external transit), but not sufficient to explain affinity flip frequency.

Investigation notes (internal):
- Hypothesis A: Account token routing metadata wrong — account-level tag (region_hint) not being honored for some in-flight sessions, causing cross-region routing and cold KV cache on remote pop.
- Hypothesis B: Rebalancer job introduced an intermediate weight change that triggered affinity re-evaluation for a subset of sessions, then some requests landed on a less warmed-up backend in us-east.
- Hypothesis C: External transit path-change caused occasional latency spikes that amplified KV-cache miss penalty (remote cache miss + cross-region RTT).

Diagnostic queries run:
- Queried routing logs for token A between 2026-03-09T21:30 and 2026-03-10T04:00 UTC — ~4.8% of requests were labeled with fallback_egress: true and routed to us-east.
- Correlated with cache hit metrics in us-east pop: affected TTLs showed lower prefix cache hits (~72% vs baseline 94%).

Temporary mitigation / workaround applied:
- Support recommended pinning Mapora account to strict eu-west affinity via account tag override (applied 2026-03-10 05:10 UTC). Post-override telemetry shows drop in cross-region routed requests to 0.3% and immediate improvement in p99 for the customer.
- Added short-term config to treat this account as high-stability for rebalancer (prevent auto-migration) while we investigate.

Resolution plan / next steps:
1) Engineering to review automated rebalancer runbook and roll back/adjust weight-change heuristics that may re-evaluate affinity for active sessions (owner: infra-routes).
2) Runtime team to instrument per-pop KV-cache warmup metrics and expose a heatmap to detect remote cold-starts on cross-region fallbacks (owner: serving-runtime).
3) SRE to correlate BGP/transit changes with routing-controller decisions to determine if external factors should suppress affinity flips (owner: network).
4) Postmortem to include customer impact and recommend change to default rebalancer aggressiveness for dedicated tenants.

Customer communication summary (to be posted):
- 2026-03-10 06:00 UTC: Acknowledged and applied account-level affinity override as temporary mitigation; asked customer to validate.
- 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC: Customer confirmed perceived latency improvements and fewer timeouts on their long-context tests.
- Will follow up with permanent fix timeline within 72h.
